claim: Bone Morphogenetic Proteins (BMPs) pattern the dorsal-ventral axis of bilaterian embryos.
source: Bone Morphogenetic Proteins (BMPs) pattern the dorsal-ventral axis of bilaterian embryos; however, their roles in the evolution of body plan are largely unknown.
evidence: This is a well-established fact in developmental biology, supported by extensive literature.

claim: BMP signaling specifies two extraembryonic tissues, the serosa and amnion, in Megaselia abdita.
source: BMP signaling specifies two extraembryonic tissues, the serosa and amnion, in basal-branching flies such as Megaselia abdita, but only one, the amnioserosa, in Drosophila melanogaster.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript, including gene expression patterns and knockdown experiments.

claim: BMP signaling specifies only one extraembryonic tissue, the amnioserosa, in Drosophila melanogaster.
source: BMP signaling specifies two extraembryonic tissues, the serosa and amnion, in basal-branching flies such as Megaselia abdita, but only one, the amnioserosa, in Drosophila melanogaster.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Drosophila development and is also referenced in the manuscript.

claim: The BMP signaling dynamics are similar in both Megaselia and Drosophila until the beginning of gastrulation.
source: The BMP signaling dynamics are similar in both species until the beginning of gastrulation, when BMP signaling broadens and intensifies at the edge of the germ rudiment in Megaselia, while remaining static in Drosophila.
evidence: This is supported by pMad staining data shown in Figure 1B and previously published work (Rafiqi et al., 2012).

claim: BMP signaling broadens and intensifies at the edge of the germ rudiment in Megaselia at the beginning of gastrulation.
source: The BMP signaling dynamics are similar in both species until the beginning of gastrulation, when BMP signaling broadens and intensifies at the edge of the germ rudiment in Megaselia, while remaining static in Drosophila.
evidence: This is demonstrated by pMad staining patterns shown in Figure 1B.

claim: BMP signaling remains static in Drosophila at the beginning of gastrulation.
source: The BMP signaling dynamics are similar in both species until the beginning of gastrulation, when BMP signaling broadens and intensifies at the edge of the germ rudiment in Megaselia, while remaining static in Drosophila.
evidence: This is demonstrated by pMad staining patterns shown in Figure 1B and is consistent with published literature.

claim: The differences in gradient dynamics and tissue specification result from evolutionary changes in the gene regulatory network that controls the activity of a positive feedback circuit on BMP signaling, involving the tumor necrosis factor alpha homolog eiger.
source: Here we show that the differences in gradient dynamics and tissue specification result from evolutionary changes in the gene regulatory network that controls the activity of a positive feedback circuit on BMP signaling, involving the tumor necrosis factor alpha homolog eiger.
evidence: This is the main finding of the manuscript, supported by multiple experiments including knockdown and overexpression studies.

claim: The BMP gradient in Drosophila melanogaster forms through directed extracellular BMP movement.
source: In Drosophila melanogaster embryos, the BMP gradient forms through directed extracellular BMP movement and initiates a positive feedback circuit leading to a bistable pattern of BMP signaling by the end of the blastoderm stage (reviewed in O'Connor et al., 2006; Shilo et al., 2013; Wharton and Serpe, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by multiple review articles cited in the manuscript.

claim: The BMP gradient in Drosophila melanogaster initiates a positive feedback circuit leading to a bistable pattern of BMP signaling by the end of the blastoderm stage.
source: In Drosophila melanogaster embryos, the BMP gradient forms through directed extracellular BMP movement and initiates a positive feedback circuit leading to a bistable pattern of BMP signaling by the end of the blastoderm stage (reviewed in O'Connor et al., 2006; Shilo et al., 2013; Wharton and Serpe, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by multiple review articles cited in the manuscript.

claim: High levels of BMP signaling, centered on the dorsal midline, specify the amnioserosa in Drosophila.
source: High levels of BMP signaling, centered on the dorsal midline, specify a single extraembryonic tissue, the amnioserosa.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Drosophila development.

claim: The dynamics of BMP signaling in the blastoderm are similar between Megaselia and Drosophila.
source: Previously, we showed that the dynamics of BMP signaling in the blastoderm are similar between Megaselia and Drosophila, but differ in the early gastrula when the Megaselia gradient broadens while the Drosophila gradient remains static (Rafiqi et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by previous work by the authors.

claim: The Megaselia BMP gradient broadens in the early gastrula while the Drosophila gradient remains static.
source: Previously, we showed that the dynamics of BMP signaling in the blastoderm are similar between Megaselia and Drosophila, but differ in the early gastrula when the Megaselia gradient broadens while the Drosophila gradient remains static (Rafiqi et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by previous work by the authors and confirmed by data in the current manuscript.

claim: Differences in the control of a positive feedback circuit involving eiger are responsible for the altered dynamics of BMP signaling and amnion specification in Megaselia.
source: Here, we show that differences in the control of a positive feedback circuit involving eiger (egr) (Gavin-Smyth et al., 2013) are responsible for the altered dynamics of BMP signaling and amnion specification in Megaselia.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the manuscript, supported by experimental data including knockdown and overexpression studies.

claim: BMP signaling can be quantified by staining with an antibody specific to the activated phosphorylated form of Mad (pMad).
source: In Megaselia and Drosophila, BMP signaling specifies extraembryonic membranes (Figure 1A) and can be quantified by staining with an antibody specific to the activated phosphorylated form of Mad (pMad), an essential transcriptional effector of the BMP pathway (Dorfman and Shilo, 2001).
evidence: This is a standard technique in the field, supported by citation.

claim: pMad is an essential transcriptional effector of the BMP pathway.
source: In Megaselia and Drosophila, BMP signaling specifies extraembryonic membranes (Figure 1A) and can be quantified by staining with an antibody specific to the activated phosphorylated form of Mad (pMad), an essential transcriptional effector of the BMP pathway (Dorfman and Shilo, 2001).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: During early blastoderm stages in both Megaselia and Drosophila, BMP signaling is initially low and broadly distributed over the dorsal regions of the embryo.
source: During early blastoderm stages in both species BMP signaling is initially low and broadly distributed over the dorsal regions of the embryo but refines into a narrow dorsal stripe of high activity by the onset of gastrulation.
evidence: This is supported by pMad staining data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: BMP signaling refines into a narrow dorsal stripe of high activity by the onset of gastrulation in both Megaselia and Drosophila.
source: During early blastoderm stages in both species BMP signaling is initially low and broadly distributed over the dorsal regions of the embryo but refines into a narrow dorsal stripe of high activity by the onset of gastrulation.
evidence: This is supported by pMad staining data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: During early gastrulation in Megaselia, the BMP signaling domain broadens to encompass the edge of the germ rudiment comprising the presumptive amnion.
source: However, during early gastrulation in Megaselia, the BMP signaling domain broadens to encompass the edge of the germ rudiment comprising the presumptive amnion, while the domain in Drosophila remains static (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by pMad staining data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The BMP signaling domain in Drosophila remains static during early gastrulation.
source: However, during early gastrulation in Megaselia, the BMP signaling domain broadens to encompass the edge of the germ rudiment comprising the presumptive amnion, while the domain in Drosophila remains static (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by pMad staining data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Mab-zen marks and specifies serosa cells in blastoderm (stage 5) and gastrula embryos (stage 6) in Megaselia.
source: A homolog of zerknüllt (Mab-zen), which encodes a homeodomain protein, marks and specifies serosa cells in blastoderm (stage 5) and gastrula embryos (stage 6) (Rafiqi et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by previous work by the authors and gene expression data.

claim: Mab-zen encodes a homeodomain protein.
source: A homolog of zerknüllt (Mab-zen), which encodes a homeodomain protein, marks and specifies serosa cells in blastoderm (stage 5) and gastrula embryos (stage 6) (Rafiqi et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the zen gene family.

claim: Mab-hnt and Mab-doc are expressed in stage 5 and 6 embryos in a slightly wider domain than Mab-zen.
source: Homologs of hindsight (Mab-hnt) and dorsocross (Mab-doc, Mab-doc2) (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1), which encode zinc-finger and T-box proteins respectively, are also expressed in stage 5 and 6 embryos in a slightly wider domain than Mab-zen (Figure 2—figure supplement 2) (Rafiqi et al., 2012), encompassing both the prospective serosa and amnion.
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data shown in figures.

claim: Mab-hnt encodes a zinc-finger protein.
source: Homologs of hindsight (Mab-hnt) and dorsocross (Mab-doc, Mab-doc2) (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1), which encode zinc-finger and T-box proteins respectively, are also expressed in stage 5 and 6 embryos in a slightly wider domain than Mab-zen (Figure 2—figure supplement 2) (Rafiqi et al., 2012), encompassing both the prospective serosa and amnion.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the hindsight gene.

claim: Mab-doc and Mab-doc2 encode T-box proteins.
source: Homologs of hindsight (Mab-hnt) and dorsocross (Mab-doc, Mab-doc2) (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1), which encode zinc-finger and T-box proteins respectively, are also expressed in stage 5 and 6 embryos in a slightly wider domain than Mab-zen (Figure 2—figure supplement 2) (Rafiqi et al., 2012), encompassing both the prospective serosa and amnion.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the dorsocross gene family.

claim: Mab-hnt and Mab-doc expression encompasses both the prospective serosa and amnion.
source: Homologs of hindsight (Mab-hnt) and dorsocross (Mab-doc, Mab-doc2) (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1), which encode zinc-finger and T-box proteins respectively, are also expressed in stage 5 and 6 embryos in a slightly wider domain than Mab-zen (Figure 2—figure supplement 2) (Rafiqi et al., 2012), encompassing both the prospective serosa and amnion.
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data shown in figures.

claim: Mab-egr is expressed in the serosa and amnion of gastrulating Megaselia embryos.
source: Lastly, a homolog of the TNF alpha gene eiger (Mab-egr) is expressed in the serosa and amnion of gastrulating Megaselia embryos (Figure 2B–C).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 2B-C.

claim: Mab-egr expression continues until dorsal closure.
source: Mab-egr expression continues until dorsal closure, but from germ band extension (stage 11) onwards it is expressed only in the amnion cells, which at this stage are polyploid and much larger than the adjacent embryonic cells (Figure 2D–E and Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data shown in figures.

claim: From germ band extension (stage 11) onwards, Mab-egr is expressed only in the amnion cells.
source: Mab-egr expression continues until dorsal closure, but from germ band extension (stage 11) onwards it is expressed only in the amnion cells, which at this stage are polyploid and much larger than the adjacent embryonic cells (Figure 2D–E and Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data shown in figures.

claim: Amnion cells at stage 11 are polyploid and much larger than the adjacent embryonic cells.
source: Mab-egr expression continues until dorsal closure, but from germ band extension (stage 11) onwards it is expressed only in the amnion cells, which at this stage are polyploid and much larger than the adjacent embryonic cells (Figure 2D–E and Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data shown in figures.

claim: In wild-type blastoderm embryos, the repression of Mab-eve extends laterally from the dorsal midline to the boundary of the Mab-zen domain.
source: In wild-type blastoderm embryos, the repression of Mab-eve extends laterally from the dorsal midline to the boundary of the Mab-zen domain, but after gastrulation begins Mab-eve expression withdraws further to abut the Mab-doc/hnt domain (Figure 2F–G and Figure 2—figure supplement 2), likely as a result of repression by BMP signaling.
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data shown in figures.

claim: After gastrulation begins, Mab-eve expression withdraws further to abut the Mab-doc/hnt domain.
source: In wild-type blastoderm embryos, the repression of Mab-eve extends laterally from the dorsal midline to the boundary of the Mab-zen domain, but after gastrulation begins Mab-eve expression withdraws further to abut the Mab-doc/hnt domain (Figure 2F–G and Figure 2—figure supplement 2), likely as a result of repression by BMP signaling.
evidence: This is supported by gene expression data shown in figures.

claim: The withdrawal of Mab-eve expression after gastrulation is likely a result of repression by BMP signaling.
source: In wild-type blastoderm embryos, the repression of Mab-eve extends laterally from the dorsal midline to the boundary of the Mab-zen domain, but after gastrulation begins Mab-eve expression withdraws further to abut the Mab-doc/hnt domain (Figure 2F–G and Figure 2—figure supplement 2), likely as a result of repression by BMP signaling.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed gene expression patterns and the known role of BMP signaling.

claim: Overexpression of Mab-eve suppresses Mab-zen expression.
source: Conversely, overexpression of Mab-eve suppresses Mab-zen expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: Amnion specification might not be completed before the onset of gastrulation.
source: Thus, amnion specification might not be completed before the onset of gastrulation.
evidence: This is inferred from the gene expression patterns observed.

claim: At stage 6, the amnion anlage of Megaselia is defined as the thin band of cells expressing Mab-doc/doc2, Mab-hnt, and Mab-egr but not Mab-zen.
source: At stage 6, the amnion anlage of Megaselia is defined as the thin band of cells expressing Mab-doc/doc2, Mab-hnt, and Mab-egr but not Mab-zen while, after germ band extension, mature amnion cells are defined by their large size and Mab-egr expression.
evidence: This is a definition based on observed gene expression patterns.

claim: After germ band extension, mature amnion cells are defined by their large size and Mab-egr expression.
source: At stage 6, the amnion anlage of Megaselia is defined as the thin band of cells expressing Mab-doc/doc2, Mab-hnt, and Mab-egr but not Mab-zen while, after germ band extension, mature amnion cells are defined by their large size and Mab-egr expression.
evidence: This is a definition based on observed morphological and gene expression characteristics.

claim: Knockdown of Mab-dpp by injection of dsRNA at the early blastoderm stage completely suppresses both serosa and amnion specification.
source: Knockdown of Mab-dpp by injection of double stranded RNA (dsRNA) at the early blastoderm stage completely suppresses both serosa and amnion specification and results in the circumferential expression of Mab-eve (Rafiqi et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by previous work by the authors.

claim: Early Mab-dpp knockdown results in the circumferential expression of Mab-eve.
source: Knockdown of Mab-dpp by injection of double stranded RNA (dsRNA) at the early blastoderm stage completely suppresses both serosa and amnion specification and results in the circumferential expression of Mab-eve (Rafiqi et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by previous work by the authors.

claim: Late Mab-dpp knockdown (after 50% blastoderm cellularization) does not affect Mab-zen expression.
source: In contrast, in all 13 late Mab-dpp knockdown embryos fixed during early gastrulation, the expression of Mab-zen was not affected; however, in five embryos the repression of Mab-eve in the amnion anlage was incomplete (Figure 2H–I).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2H-I.

claim: Late Mab-dpp knockdown results in incomplete repression of Mab-eve in the amnion anlage in some embryos.
source: In contrast, in all 13 late Mab-dpp knockdown embryos fixed during early gastrulation, the expression of Mab-zen was not affected; however, in five embryos the repression of Mab-eve in the amnion anlage was incomplete (Figure 2H–I).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2H-I.

claim: Late Mab-dpp knockdown reduced Mab-egr expression in a majority of stage 11/12 embryos (55%, n = 40).
source: Late Mab-dpp knockdown reduced Mab-egr expression in a majority of stage 11/12 embryos (55%, n = 40) whereas late ectopic Mab-dpp expression caused an expansion of the Mab-egr domain in at least 35% of the embryos (n = 57) (Figure 2J–L).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2J-L.

claim: Late ectopic Mab-dpp expression caused an expansion of the Mab-egr domain in at least 35% of the embryos (n = 57).
source: Late Mab-dpp knockdown reduced Mab-egr expression in a majority of stage 11/12 embryos (55%, n = 40) whereas late ectopic Mab-dpp expression caused an expansion of the Mab-egr domain in at least 35% of the embryos (n = 57) (Figure 2J–L).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2J-L.

claim: BMP signaling during gastrulation is necessary and sufficient for amnion specification.
source: Taken together, these data provide evidence that BMP signaling during gastrulation is necessary and sufficient for amnion specification.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented, including knockdown and overexpression experiments.

claim: In Drosophila, both BMP signaling and zen are necessary at the blastoderm stage for the expression of the three doc paralogs and hnt in the amnioserosa anlage.
source: In Drosophila, both BMP signaling and zen are necessary at the blastoderm stage for the expression of the three doc paralogs and hnt in the amnioserosa anlage, although the essential function of these genes in amnioserosa maintenance becomes apparent only after gastrulation (Yip et al., 1997; Reim et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The essential function of doc and hnt genes in amnioserosa maintenance becomes apparent only after gastrulation in Drosophila.
source: In Drosophila, both BMP signaling and zen are necessary at the blastoderm stage for the expression of the three doc paralogs and hnt in the amnioserosa anlage, although the essential function of these genes in amnioserosa maintenance becomes apparent only after gastrulation (Yip et al., 1997; Reim et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: In Megaselia, BMP signaling activates Mab-doc and Mab-hnt independently from Mab-zen.
source: However, in Megaselia, BMP signaling activates Mab-doc and Mab-hnt independently from Mab-zen (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–I), suggesting these genes could play a role in amnion specification.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-I.

claim: Mab-doc and Mab-hnt could play a role in amnion specification in Megaselia.
source: However, in Megaselia, BMP signaling activates Mab-doc and Mab-hnt independently from Mab-zen (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–I), suggesting these genes could play a role in amnion specification.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the observed gene expression patterns.

claim: Knockdown of Mab-doc/doc2 or Mab-hnt results in confluent expression domains of Mab-zen and Mab-eve during early gastrulation.
source: Following knockdown of Mab-doc/doc2 or Mab-hnt activity by RNAi, we observed confluent expression domains of Mab-zen and Mab-eve during early gastrulation (4/9 and 5/11 embryos, respectively; Figure 3A–C), and a decrease in Mab-egr expression at stage 11/12 (Figure 3D–F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A-C.

claim: Knockdown of Mab-doc/doc2 or Mab-hnt results in a decrease in Mab-egr expression at stage 11/12.
source: Following knockdown of Mab-doc/doc2 or Mab-hnt activity by RNAi, we observed confluent expression domains of Mab-zen and Mab-eve during early gastrulation (4/9 and 5/11 embryos, respectively; Figure 3A–C), and a decrease in Mab-egr expression at stage 11/12 (Figure 3D–F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D-F.

claim: Knockdown of the activities of Mab-doc/doc2, Mab-hnt, and Mab-zen together eliminated Mab-egr expression in germ-band extended embryos.
source: Knockdown of the activities of all three genes eliminated Mab-egr expression in germ-band extended embryos (Figure 3D), indicating that Mab-doc/doc2 and Mab-hnt together are essential for amnion specification in Megaselia.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Mab-doc/doc2 and Mab-hnt together are essential for amnion specification in Megaselia.
source: Knockdown of the activities of all three genes eliminated Mab-egr expression in germ-band extended embryos (Figure 3D), indicating that Mab-doc/doc2 and Mab-hnt together are essential for amnion specification in Megaselia.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Overexpression of Mab-doc or Mab-hnt induced ectopic amnion, as evidenced by an enlargement of the Mab-egr domain at stage 11/12.
source: Conversely, overexpression of Mab-doc or Mab-hnt induced ectopic amnion, as evidenced by an enlargement of the Mab-egr domain at stage 11/12 (Figure 3G and Figure 3—figure supplement 1J–L).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3G and Figure 3—figure supplement 1J-L.

claim: Overexpression of Mab-doc could bypass the requirement for Mab-hnt.
source: Overexpression of Mab-doc could bypass the requirement for Mab-hnt, while overexpression of Mab-hnt could not bypass the requirement for Mab-doc (Figure 3—figure supplement 1M–N), consistent with the hypothesis that Mab-doc and Mab-hnt share a common target necessary for amnion formation that is primarily dependent upon doc activity.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1M-N.

claim: Overexpression of Mab-hnt could not bypass the requirement for Mab-doc.
source: Overexpression of Mab-doc could bypass the requirement for Mab-hnt, while overexpression of Mab-hnt could not bypass the requirement for Mab-doc (Figure 3—figure supplement 1M–N), consistent with the hypothesis that Mab-doc and Mab-hnt share a common target necessary for amnion formation that is primarily dependent upon doc activity.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1M-N.

claim: Mab-doc and Mab-hnt share a common target necessary for amnion formation that is primarily dependent upon doc activity.
source: Overexpression of Mab-doc could bypass the requirement for Mab-hnt, while overexpression of Mab-hnt could not bypass the requirement for Mab-doc (Figure 3—figure supplement 1M–N), consistent with the hypothesis that Mab-doc and Mab-hnt share a common target necessary for amnion formation that is primarily dependent upon doc activity.
evidence: This is a hypothesis consistent with the experimental data.

claim: Overexpression of Mab-doc in Mab-dpp knockdown embryos did not induce any expression of Mab-egr in stage 11/12 embryos (n = 44).
source: Overexpression of Mab-doc in Mab-dpp knockdown embryos did not induce any expression of Mab-egr in stage 11/12 embryos (n = 44) (Figure 3H).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3H.

claim: Overexpression of Mab-dpp in Mab-doc/doc2 knockdown embryos resulted in ectopic expression of Mab-egr at stage 11/12 (36%, n = 47).
source: Conversely, overexpression of Mab-dpp in Mab-doc/doc2 knockdown embryos resulted in ectopic expression of Mab-egr at stage 11/12 (36%, n = 47) (Figure 3I).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3I.

claim: BMP signaling is sufficient to direct the expression of amnion specific genes in the absence of Mab-doc/doc2 activity.
source: Thus, BMP signaling is sufficient to direct the expression of amnion specific genes in the absence of Mab-doc/doc2 activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing that overexpression of Mab-dpp can induce Mab-egr expression even when Mab-doc/doc2 is knocked down.

claim: Knockdown of Mab-zen partially restored amnion in Mab-doc/doc2 knockdown embryos.
source: Knockdown of Mab-zen partially restored amnion in Mab-doc/doc2 knockdown embryos (Figure 3—figure supplement 1O).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1O.

claim: The endogenous level of BMP signaling at the dorsal midline in the blastoderm embryo is sufficient to specify amnion in the absence of both Mab-doc/doc2 and Mab-zen.
source: To confirm that this result was not due to an excessive non-physiological level of Mab-Dpp produced by the injected mRNA, we asked whether the endogenous level of BMP signaling at the dorsal midline in the blastoderm embryo would be sufficient to specify amnion in the absence of both Mab-doc/doc2 and the serosal determinant Mab-zen. Knockdown of Mab-zen partially restored amnion in Mab-doc/doc2 knockdown embryos (Figure 3—figure supplement 1O).
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental result showing partial restoration of amnion when Mab-zen is knocked down in Mab-doc/doc2 knockdown embryos.

claim: Mab-doc promotes amnion formation permissively.
source: Taken together, these data suggest Mab-doc promotes amnion formation permissively.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing that BMP signaling is sufficient for amnion specification even without Mab-doc.

claim: Mab-doc/doc2 knockdown had little effect on pMad levels during the late blastoderm stage compared to control embryos (Wilcoxon rank sum test, p=0.3697).
source: While Mab-doc/doc2 knockdown had little effect on pMad levels during the late blastoderm stage compared to control embryos (Wilcoxon rank sum test, p=0.3697; Figure 3J), in early gastrula stage embryos, knockdown of Mab-doc/doc2 resulted in significantly reduced pMad levels compared to control embryos (Wilcoxon rank sum test, p=0.01165; Figure 3K).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative pMad staining data shown in Figure 3J.

claim: In early gastrula stage embryos, knockdown of Mab-doc/doc2 resulted in significantly reduced pMad levels compared to control embryos (Wilcoxon rank sum test, p=0.01165).
source: While Mab-doc/doc2 knockdown had little effect on pMad levels during the late blastoderm stage compared to control embryos (Wilcoxon rank sum test, p=0.3697; Figure 3J), in early gastrula stage embryos, knockdown of Mab-doc/doc2 resulted in significantly reduced pMad levels compared to control embryos (Wilcoxon rank sum test, p=0.01165; Figure 3K).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative pMad staining data shown in Figure 3K.

claim: Knockdown of Mab-zen did not alter the average level of pMad at the beginning of gastrulation (Wilcoxon rank sum test, p=0.2367).
source: In contrast, knockdown of Mab-zen did not alter the average level of pMad at the beginning of gastrulation (Wilcoxon rank sum test, p=0.2367; Figure 3L).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative pMad staining data shown in Figure 3L.

claim: Mab-doc/doc2 is dispensable for amnion cell fate specification but necessary for wild-type levels of BMP signaling at the early gastrula stage.
source: The observation that Mab-doc/doc2 is dispensable for amnion cell fate specification but necessary for wild-type levels of BMP signaling at the early gastrula stage strongly support the model that amnion formation is driven by a Mab-doc-dependent elevation of BMP signaling in the amnion anlage at the onset of gastrulation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Amnion formation is driven by a Mab-doc-dependent elevation of BMP signaling in the amnion anlage at the onset of gastrulation.
source: The observation that Mab-doc/doc2 is dispensable for amnion cell fate specification but necessary for wild-type levels of BMP signaling at the early gastrula stage strongly support the model that amnion formation is driven by a Mab-doc-dependent elevation of BMP signaling in the amnion anlage at the onset of gastrulation.
evidence: This is a model supported by the experimental data.

claim: Embryos injected centrally with Mab-doc mRNA displayed a local expansion of the pMad domain during gastrulation (15/15).
source: Embryos injected centrally with Mab-doc mRNA displayed a local expansion of the pMad domain during gastrulation (15/15) coupled with the frequent depletion of endogenous pMad in adjacent regions (12/15) (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Embryos injected centrally with Mab-doc mRNA frequently showed depletion of endogenous pMad in adjacent regions (12/15).
source: Embryos injected centrally with Mab-doc mRNA displayed a local expansion of the pMad domain during gastrulation (15/15) coupled with the frequent depletion of endogenous pMad in adjacent regions (12/15) (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Injection of mRNA encoding activated BMP receptors into the Drosophila blastoderm embryo causes an increase in BMP ligand-receptor interactions, coupled with a decrease in BMP ligand-receptor binding in nearby regions.
source: This result parallels a phenotype observed in Drosophila where injection of mRNA encoding activated BMP receptors into the blastoderm embryo causes an increase in BMP ligand-receptor interactions, coupled with a decrease in BMP ligand-receptor binding in nearby regions (Wang and Ferguson, 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: A positive feedback circuit downstream of BMP signaling increases local receptor-ligand interactions.
source: These data indicate that a positive feedback circuit downstream of BMP signaling increases local receptor-ligand interactions, and that, due to a limiting amount of BMP ligand, ligand-receptor interactions decrease in nearby regions.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental observations.

claim: Due to a limiting amount of BMP ligand, ligand-receptor interactions decrease in nearby regions when a positive feedback circuit is activated locally.
source: These data indicate that a positive feedback circuit downstream of BMP signaling increases local receptor-ligand interactions, and that, due to a limiting amount of BMP ligand, ligand-receptor interactions decrease in nearby regions.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental observations.

claim: Megaselia embryos injected with Mab-zen mRNA (n = 11) had a similar pMad domain to injected control embryos (n = 12).
source: Conversely, Megaselia embryos injected with Mab-zen mRNA (n = 11) had a similar pMad domain to injected control embryos (n = 12) and developed a reduced or abnormal amnion (44/51) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Megaselia embryos injected with Mab-zen mRNA developed a reduced or abnormal amnion (44/51).

claim: Positive feedback circuits can be an important target in the evolution of body plans.
